Oil and gas NDT training in Deer Park: what you need to know first

Deer Park oil and gas NDT training covers ASNT SNT-TC-1A Level I, II and III methods (UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET) for work on the refinery, chemical plants and bulk-liquid tank terminals along the Houston Ship Channel. Atlantis NDT runs it live online or onsite at your Deer Park facility, with ASNT Level III oversight. Your employer certifies you to its written practice. Radiographers also need a Texas DSHS certification. There is no Atlantis classroom in Deer Park.

This page is for the people who keep Deer Park's tanks, pipe racks and process units inspected: terminal integrity coordinators, contractor operations managers, and technicians working toward Level II. It focuses on what is specific to Deer Park, which is mostly storage and transfer, rather than repeating the general Houston story.

Oil and gas NDT work in Deer Park

Deer Park's industrial frontage runs along the south bank of the ship channel, north of Highway 225. Three kinds of assets shape the NDT work there. We name them as context only; none of them is presented as an Atlantis client.

  • An integrated refinery and chemical site. The Deer Park refinery has been fully owned by PEMEX since 2022, when Shell sold its share of the joint venture. Shell still owns and operates the neighbouring Deer Park chemical plant. Two operators on one integrated site means two sets of owner standards, contractor approvals and inspection programmes that a contractor may need to work under.
  • Bulk-liquid storage terminals. Deer Park has some of the densest tank storage on the channel. Large terminal operators run hundreds of aboveground tanks, plus manifolds, docks and transfer piping. The March 2019 tank-farm fire at the Intercontinental Terminals Company site in Deer Park made tank integrity, secondary containment and transfer-line condition a lasting public concern.
  • Specialty chemical and additive plants. Smaller chemical producers along the channel add their own vessels, reactors and stainless piping.

That mix makes Deer Park more tank-heavy than any other market we cover in the Houston area. A technician here spends a large share of the year on tank shells, floors, nozzles and roofs, on terminal piping that cycles between products, and on dock lines exposed to salt air. Refinery turnaround work comes on top of that.

Methods and their Deer Park applications

MethodDeer Park oil and gas applicationCode or standard (context)
UT thicknessTank shell courses, nozzle necks, and terminal transfer and manifold piping thickness surveysOwner API 653 and API 570 programmes; ASME Section V Article 23 (SE-797)
UT shear waveRepair and alteration welds on tanks and piping; nozzle reinforcement weldsASME Section V Article 4; API 650 for new tank construction
PAUTCorrosion mapping on shell plates and under repads; weld examination on refinery repairsASME Section V Article 4; owner procedures
TOFDSizing indications in thicker refinery vessel and column weldsASME Section V Article 4
RTShell-to-shell and piping welds on new tanks, repairs and refinery tie-insAPI 650 and 653 radiography rules; ASME Section V Article 2; Texas DSHS rules
MTShell-to-bottom welds, nozzle welds and repair excavations on carbon-steel tanksASME Section V Article 7
PTStainless chemical-plant welds and tank appurtenances where MT does not applyASME Section V Article 6
VTExternal tank and foundation condition, welds, coatings, roof and seal componentsASME Section V Article 9; owner tank checklists
ETExchanger tubing at refinery turnaround; surface cracking on coated weldsASME Section V Article 8

Method spotlight for Deer Park: UT for tank and terminal integrity. Most tank inspection in Deer Park depends on getting thickness and weld UT right on the shell: correct couplant and surface preparation on painted plates, telling a lamination from wall loss, sizing pitting near the chime, and recording readings so an API 653 inspector can actually calculate remaining life from them. Our UT Level II course can be built around tank work when delivered onsite, and phased array training covers corrosion mapping. Tank-floor scanning with magnetic flux leakage is common in terminals. It is usually qualified on the scanner supplier's equipment under the employer's written practice. Ask us about it if your written practice covers MFL; we will not pretend a generic course replaces that equipment-specific qualification.

The SNT-TC-1A route for Deer Park technicians

  1. Get hired or sponsored. SNT-TC-1A certification is employer-based, so the first step is almost always a contractor or plant that will certify you. Our guide to employer sponsorship explains how that works from the company's side.
  2. Follow the employer's written practice. It sets training and experience hours, exam rules and recertification for each method. Companies without one can use our written practice development service.
  3. Complete formal training. Method theory, technique, applicable codes and safety. Compare minimum hours on the training requirements matrix.
  4. Log supervised experience. Tank outages and terminal campaigns build hours quickly, but only if they are documented properly.
  5. Pass general, specific and practical exams set or overseen by a Level III, with the practical done on real specimens.
  6. Pass the eye tests for near vision and colour contrast. Near vision is retested every year, which matters when you read faint thickness displays in bright sun on a tank roof.
  7. Receive employer certification and keep it current through the recertification cycle in the written practice.

See also the SNT-TC-1A certification guide and the Level I and Level II pages.

Radiation licensing, TWIC and badging in Deer Park

Texas is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography in Deer Park is regulated by the Texas Department of State Health Services Radiation Control program under 25 TAC §289.255. The rule says a licensee may not let anyone act as a radiographer without a valid radiographer certification. Getting one involves a training course that meets the rule's requirements, supervised on-the-job work as a radiographer trainee under a radiographer trainer, and a state application. DSHS certification ID cards are valid for five years. Always confirm current requirements with DSHS before planning.

For training planning, keep two tracks separate: RT method training for SNT-TC-1A (technique, film or digital interpretation, codes) and the state radiation-safety certification that lets someone operate sources. A strong RT Level II who has not completed the DSHS process still cannot lead a shot in Deer Park.

Access is the other practical constraint. Terminals with marine docks on the channel are regulated under maritime security rules and need TWIC for unescorted entry. Refinery and chemical sites in Deer Park generally require a contractor safety orientation before issuing a badge. The Houston Area Safety Council's Basic Orientation Plus is widely used in the area. Some owners also require site-specific orientations and drug and alcohol testing.

How Deer Park crews can be trained

  • Live online sessions for theory, codes and procedure reviews. Useful when terminal staff work rotating shifts and cannot all be released at once. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility, which can be a terminal maintenance building, a contractor yard off Highway 225 or a refinery training room. Practicals use your own thickness gauges, flaw detectors and tank-plate samples, so the training matches the work.
  • Blended programmes that put theory before a tank-cleaning window or refinery turnaround and do the practicals and exams onsite once tanks or units are back in service.

Terminal work in Deer Park runs all year, but refinery turnarounds still cause staffing peaks. We schedule training around both. Send us your tank-outage or turnaround calendar and we will propose dates.

Employer services: Level III and written practices in Deer Park

Tank inspection companies grow quickly and often end up with technicians certified under an older written practice that no longer matches their current scope, such as corrosion mapping or MFL floor scanning. When an owner audits a contractor, the first documents requested are the written practice, certification records, exam papers and vision records. Atlantis can:

  • Bring your written practice up to date with the methods and techniques your crews really use.
  • Write, administer and grade Level I and II exams.
  • Serve as your outside Level III. See Level III of record in Deer Park.
  • Support advanced UT procedures. See UT Level III support in Deer Park.

Owner-side programme work is covered on NDT consulting in Deer Park and refining NDT consulting in Deer Park. For multi-site group training, see corporate NDT training. Book a Level III consultation for your Deer Park company.

What a Deer Park terminal or contractor receives

When a Deer Park employer books a cohort, the deliverables are the records an owner auditor will ask for, not just a certificate of attendance:

  • A training outline mapped to the methods and levels in your written practice, with the codes your crews work to (API 653 and 570 owner programmes, ASME Section V, API 650 for new construction).
  • Attendance and hours records for each technician, in a format that drops straight into certification files.
  • Written general and specific exams, graded and filed, with the specific exam built around your own procedures and tank or piping acceptance criteria.
  • Practical exams on real specimens, ideally with flaws or wall loss typical of tank shells and terminal piping, documented with the checklist your Level III signs.
  • A gap note listing anything in your written practice or procedures that an owner audit is likely to question.

This record-first approach suits Deer Park in particular. Terminal operators prequalify contractors through owner audits and contractor-management platforms, and missing exam records are a common reason a crew is held at the gate.

Practise before the practical exam

Trainees can rehearse in the Practical NDT simulator, which covers 12 methods across 5 environments. Its storage-tank and oil and gas site environments are the closest to Deer Park work. Use it to practise scan coverage, probe orientation and indication recognition between sessions. It is practice only. Your practical exam is still done on real specimens, and simulator time is not on-the-job experience.

Your instructor

Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, leads the training and Level III services. Technicians working toward the top level can use our ASNT Level III exam preparation.

Deer Park NDT training options compared

  • San Jacinto College. San Jac, next door in Pasadena, runs an Inspection Technologies programme with an NDT certificate, a Level 2 certificate path and an associate degree, plus a separate fixed-equipment inspection track. Classes are offered in the evenings and on Saturdays. It is the obvious choice for Deer Park residents who want a college programme. Confirm current offerings with the college.
  • Houston classroom schools. Several established NDT schools in the Houston area run open-enrolment classroom courses on a published schedule.
  • Contractor in-house training. Many tank and refinery inspection contractors train their own helpers and trainees.
  • Atlantis NDT. We are not a walk-in school. We fit best when a Deer Park terminal operator or contractor wants a crew trained together to its own written practice, at its own site or live online, with Level III exam support built in.

Deer Park oil and gas NDT training: frequently asked questions

Is there oil and gas NDT training in Deer Park, TX?

Yes, in several forms: college programmes nearby, Houston classroom schools, contractor in-house training, and employer-arranged training from Atlantis, delivered live online or onsite at a Deer Park facility. Atlantis has no classroom in Deer Park.

How do I become an NDT technician in Deer Park?

Most people start as a helper or trainee with an inspection contractor, then complete formal training and supervised experience and pass exams under the employer's SNT-TC-1A written practice. See how to become an NDT technician.

What NDT is used on storage tanks in Deer Park?

Mostly UT thickness and weld examination on shells and nozzles, VT, MT on carbon-steel welds, and RT on new or repaired shell welds. Terminals also use floor-scanning techniques such as MFL. The tank inspector who signs off usually holds API 653, which is a separate credential.

Will NDT training make me an API 653 inspector?

No. API 653 is an inspector certification earned through API's own eligibility and exam process. NDT training prepares you to collect the data that inspector uses. Atlantis does not offer API inspector training.

Do I need a Texas license to do radiography in Deer Park?

Yes. Under 25 TAC §289.255, you need a valid Texas DSHS radiographer certification to act as a radiographer, and your employer needs the corresponding radiation licence or registration. That is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT certification.

Can I do NDT training online in Texas?

Yes for the classroom portion. Practical exams and on-the-job experience still have to be completed hands-on.

How long does it take to get UT Level II for tank work?

That depends on your employer's written practice and your starting level. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum training and experience hours that employers can adjust with documented justification. The training requirements matrix lays them out, and our UT Level 2 practice questions help with exam preparation.

How much does NDT training cost for a Deer Park crew?

We quote on request. The main factors are the methods and levels, the number of technicians, online or onsite delivery, and whether you also want exam administration or written-practice work. We usually send cohort and onsite quotes within one business day. Request a Deer Park training quote.

Can I use WIOA or GI Bill benefits?

Only at providers approved for those programmes. Texas WIOA funding runs through Workforce Solutions boards and their eligible provider list, and GI Bill funding requires a VA-approved programme. Atlantis does not claim those approvals. Most Deer Park technicians are trained at their employer's expense.

Do Deer Park terminals require TWIC?

Facilities with marine docks under maritime security rules require TWIC for unescorted access. Expect a contractor safety orientation and site-specific requirements too.

Can you train our technicians at our Deer Park terminal?

Yes. Onsite delivery using your equipment and procedures is our standard model for terminal and contractor crews. Ask about onsite training for your Deer Park crew.

What are NDT salaries like near Deer Park?

They vary with method, level, overtime and turnaround work, and we do not publish unsourced local numbers. See our NDT salary guide.
